description: Owed by bedrock-q67.20.2: the bootstrap shard_key decode keeps a narrow binary_to_term(value, [:safe]) fallback (materializer_bootstrap_phase.ex decode_legacy_shard_tag) for clusters that wrote shard keys before Bedrock.SystemKeys.Values. RETIREMENT MECHANISM CHANGED by bedrock-q67.21.2 (2026-08-21): recovery no longer rewrites shard_keys/ for existing clusters (read-and-heal), so legacy values are NEVER re-encoded by recoveries — the original 'every completed recovery re-encodes; remove one release after 0.7' plan is dead. Retiring the fallback now requires an explicit one-time migration (a system transaction re-encoding legacy entries — natural home: the distributor's first ownership pass, or a dedicated migration step), after which the fallback and the adjacency reconstruction inside it can be deleted. A legacy family stays encoding-uniform meanwhile (nothing rewrites it), which the any-legacy-falls-back-whole rule covers.

comments.text:
INVALID as scoped — closing without a PR.

Census confirms the ticket's own analysis: the fallback lives in lib/bedrock/system_keys/reader.ex (decode_legacy_shard_tag/shard_layout_from_entries, not materializer_bootstrap_phase.ex — it moved there during q67.21.13's tag-0-only rework, but is the same code the ticket names).

1. WRITERS are canonical: both call sites that write shard_key values (materializer_bootstrap_phase.ex:191 and routing_data.ex ~286) call Values.encode_shard_key_entry/2, the SystemKeys.Values tuple-encoding introduced by bedrock-ri40/q67.20.2. No writer anywhere in lib/ uses term_to_binary for shard_key values.

2. NO MIGRATION EXISTS to re-encode already-persisted legacy entries. grep -rl migrat lib/ turns up zero migration code for this family (the other 'migration' hits are the unrelated log-window migration and the system-materializer bootstrap-record migration). The distributor's startup_sweep (control_plane/distributor/server.ex:118) only reads a snapshot and heals coverage gaps — it never rewrites shard_keys/ entries.

3. LEGACY RECORDS CAN STILL REACH PRODUCTION: bedrock-q67.21.2 shipped read-and-heal recovery — shard_keys/ seeds only-when-absent and is never rewritten for an existing cluster (system_keys/reader.ex:88-94 documents this explicitly: 'recovery no longer rewrites the family... so a legacy family stays legacy... until bedrock-q67.20.7 retires the fallback with an explicit migration'). This killed the original retirement plan bedrock-q67.20.2 relied on ('every completed recovery re-encodes; remove one release after 0.7'). Unlike the single-valued materializer shape (q67.21.22, closed as never-shipped), this legacy shard-key format DID ship in real pre-Values clusters and has no rewrite path.

Per the ticket-protocol INVALID criterion: a legacy record can still reach a cluster and no migration exists, so retiring the fallback now would silently break any pre-Values cluster's shard layout. Closing without code changes. The natural follow-up (an explicit one-time migration — distributor's first ownership pass or a dedicated migration step, as the ticket itself suggests) is a separate P-task the epic owner should file if still wanted; not filed here per protocol (evidence-only close, no scope creep).

title: Remove legacy term_to_binary shard-tag fallback from materializer bootstrap
